name: vLLM compilation and custom-op strategy
scope: Read vLLM at commit 76081b9 (2026-10-16) under agent_space/vllm. Files covered: vllm/compilation (backends.split_graph, partition_rules, piecewise_backend compile ranges, cuda_graph wrapper, breakable_cudagraph), vllm/compilation/passes (pass_manager, noop_elimination, the fusion/* passes, the ir/ lowering and clone elimination), the vLLM IR (vllm/ir/op.py, vllm/ir/ops/layernorm.py), CustomOp and direct_register_custom_op, the stateful mixer ops (mamba_mixer2), config/compilation.py (splitting_ops, _attention_ops, capture sizes, PassConfig), config/vllm.py (optimization levels, enable_* predicates, _set_cudagraph_sizes), the Transformers-backend dataflow fusers (models/transformers/fuser.py, fusers/*), v1 CudagraphDispatcher and AttentionCGSupport, and docs/design/{fusions,cuda_graphs,vllm_ir}.md. Git history shows the torch.compile sequence-parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed on 2026-10-08 (commit 194bd72be7, PR #60517); they were read from the parent commit. These were compared with MegaBake's regions.py, lowering.py (declared ops), fx_handler/hf_attention.py, buckets.py, bodies/gemm.py, planner.py, schedule.py, compiler.py, ROADMAP.md, PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md, and the fresh benchmark reports in artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18. Questions answered for MegaBake: (1) how vLLM keeps one compiler path general across hundreds of models; (2) which of its mechanisms MegaBake should copy; (3) which vLLM limits come from running many kernels, where a single persistent kernel can do better; (4) which MegaBake constants and matchers look fitted to the tested models or to the 60-SM MIG slice.

core_ideas.idea: Declared opaque custom ops for stateful/complex mixers (splitting ops)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each stateful mixer (attention, mamba_mixer2, short_conv, linear_attention, qwen_gdn_attention_core, sparse indexer, ...) is registered with direct_register_custom_op. The schema is inferred from a Python function that takes the activations, a preallocated output buffer marked in mutates_args, and a layer_name string. At run time the op looks up the layer object (which owns the KV/SSM state and the attention metadata) in forward_context.no_compile_layers. Dynamo and Inductor see one functional node with a fake implementation, so model code compiles with fullgraph. The state stays invisible to the compiler. These ops' names make up the default splitting_ops list.

core_ideas.idea: Piecewise compilation and piecewise CUDA graphs (graph split at splitting ops)
core_ideas.how_it_works: split_graph walks the Dynamo FX graph and gives each splitting-op node its own submodule, keeping consecutive splitting ops together. getitem nodes stay with their producer. Each non-splitting piece is compiled by Inductor and wrapped in a CUDAGraphWrapper. The splitting ops run eagerly between graph replays, so attention backends with dynamic metadata still work. Alternatives: Inductor graph partition (custom_should_partition_ops or the cudagraph_unsafe tag), which splits after all fusion passes so fullgraph-only fusions still apply, and breakable CUDA graphs, which end stream capture at the dispatcher around such ops.

core_ideas.idea: Dual-mode CUDA graphs (FULL for uniform decode, PIECEWISE for mixed) with capability-based downgrade
core_ideas.how_it_works: A FULL wrapper wraps the whole model and PIECEWISE wrappers wrap each piece. CudagraphDispatcher keeps two sets of BatchDescriptor keys (num_tokens, num_reqs, uniform, lora) and picks FULL > PIECEWISE > NONE for the padded batch. Each attention backend declares AttentionCGSupport. The model takes the minimum across its backends, and the mode is downgraded to fit (for example FULL to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE).

core_ideas.idea: Model-agnostic capture-size ladder and compile ranges
core_ideas.how_it_works: The default capture sizes are [1,2,4] + range(8,256,8) + range(256,max+1,16), with max = min(2*max_num_seqs*decode_query_len, 512, or 1024 on SM100) capped by max_num_batched_tokens. max_num_batched_tokens and the uniform spec-decode sizes are added. A batch is padded to the next captured size, and runs eagerly above the largest. Separately, compile_ranges_endpoints split the token axis into ranges, each compiled once with a dynamic shape; compile_sizes add single-size specializations. Every input is an engine-level quantity (scheduler limits, spec-decode width, device family). None is a model shape.

Every InductorPass can refuse a compile range. AllReduceFusionPass applies only when range.end <= max_token_num, which comes from a per-capability, per-world-size MB table. The old SP pass added a compile-range endpoint at its token threshold. The pass manager skips inapplicable passes per range, and the range is part of the cache uuid.

core_ideas.idea: vLLM IR: semantic ops with late, priority-based lowering
core_ideas.how_it_works: @vllm.ir.register_op declares an op such as rms_norm or fused_add_rms_norm by its native PyTorch reference, with an input generator and per-dtype tolerances. Providers (vllm_c, aiter, triton, oink, helion) register implementations with a static supported flag and a supports_args(shape/dtype) predicate. The model calls the IR op, so the FX graph holds one node per semantic op. Fusion passes match that single node and not decomposed aten. After fusion, VllmIRLoweringPass dispatches each remaining node through a priority list to the first provider whose supports_args accepts its fake args, then inlines that provider with replace_by_example. Priorities and implementation source hashes are part of the cache key. The design doc names autotuning over implementations as future work.

core_ideas.idea: CustomOp dual forms (forward_native vs forward_cuda) and matchers covering both
core_ideas.how_it_works: A CustomOp layer has per-platform forwards. custom_ops '+op'/'-op'/'all'/'none' chooses the hand kernel or the native torch code, which Inductor then fuses itself. Each MatcherCustomOp in fusion passes produces either the custom-op pattern or the native pattern, so a fusion fires on either form. The fusion docs say that on NVIDIA, Inductor's generated RMSNorm+quant and SiLU+quant kernels beat vLLM's custom ones, so those fusions are enabled only when the custom op is active.

core_ideas.idea: Pattern-replacement fusion passes (RMSNorm+quant, add+RMSNorm, SiLU*mul+quant, attention+quant, QK-norm+RoPE, RoPE+KV-cache write, AllReduce+RMSNorm(+quant))
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each pass registers pattern and replacement functions with Inductor's pattern matcher. They are traced with fwd_only on tiny bf16 example tensors (e.g. (5,16)) and become graph patterns that are symbolic in shape. A replacement calls a hand-written fused kernel through auto_functionalized, e.g. fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant or FlashInfer trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm. Extra checks such as matching input/weight dtype guard the match. Scalar constants are not wildcards: epsilon is enumerated over [1e-5, 1e-6] and one pattern is registered per value. Group-quant patterns are enumerated over group shape, scale layout, e8m0 and TMA alignment.

tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce followed by rms_norm or fused_add_rms_norm is replaced by FlashInfer's fused one-shot/two-shot allreduce kernel. The kernel uses an IPC workspace and does the reduction, residual add, norm and optional FP8/NVFP4 quant in one launch. It is profitable only for small token counts, so it is gated by FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB[capability][world_size], with values from 0.5 MB to 64 MB.

Before removal: allreduce -> RMSNorm was rewritten to reduce_scatter -> RMSNorm on 1/TP of the tokens -> all_gather. AsyncTP then fused the all_gather/reduce_scatter with the neighboring GEMMs (collective matmul). It was enabled only above token thresholds derived from SP_MIN_HIDDEN_SIZE (8192 on SM90/SM100) and SP_MIN_PER_GPU_SIZE_MB (8 MB on SM90, 32 MB on SM100). Commit 194bd72be7 deleted both passes and about 1,600 lines of their implementation. The message gives no reason. [uncertain] A likely reason is maintenance cost relative to gains that were only present for large hidden sizes.

Reshape chains are collapsed onto the base tensor. reshape, slice and slice_scatter nodes whose output shape equals their input shape are removed, with dims compared by statically_known_true on SymInts. This exposes 2D patterns for later fusions. The fusion flags fail validation if eliminate_noops is off. Later steps run PostCleanup (DCE), UnsafeCloneElimination and FixFunctionalization, which turns auto_functionalized nodes back into in-place calls so no copies are added.

core_ideas.idea: Transformers-backend dataflow fusers (generic module rewriting for arbitrary HF models)
core_ideas.how_it_works: For every module class, vLLM FX-traces the module once. The result is cached on (class, child names). Fusers match by dataflow and not by class name: RMSNormFuser for leaf modules computing RMSNorm, GLUFuser for act(gate(x))*up(x) (it AST-rewrites forward to act(gate_up(x)) with merged weights), QKVFuser and PackedQKVFuser for sibling q/k/v linears that share an input (one merged projection plus a split), MergedColumnParallelFuser, and AttentionFuser. A module named *RMSNorm that does not match produces a warning. Then post-grad passes canonicalize: residual add + rms_norm becomes fused_add_rms_norm (AddRMSNormFusionPass), and the post-norm flatten is hoisted (RMSNormReshapeFusionPass).

Each level maps PassConfig flags to booleans or to predicates evaluated on VllmConfig: is the custom op enabled, TP>1 with SM90/SM100 and flashinfer installed, is the model NVFP4, ROCm AITER, and even hidden_size == 2880 for the gpt-oss norm-pad fusion. User overrides take precedence. One code path then serves all models, with fusions switched on by hardware and model properties and not per model.

core_ideas.idea: Cache keys that include the pass pipeline
core_ideas.how_it_works: PostGradPassManager.uuid hashes the PassConfig, every pass's uuid (source hash), the IR priority lists and implementation hashes, and the compile range. CompilationConfig.compute_hash covers everything that changes the graph. Any change to passes or kernel choice invalidates the cached Inductor artifacts.

megabake_status.idea: Declared opaque custom ops for stateful/complex mixers
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/lowering.py:211-306 (megabake::kv_attention, megabake::attention); fx_handler/hf_attention.py:64-71 (AttentionInterface); ROADMAP step 6 (gated delta rule) not started; artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18/Qwen--Qwen3.5-0.8B/report.json fails on aten.cumsum and linalg_solve_triangular
megabake_status.notes: Better than vLLM in one respect: the state (key_cache, value_cache, valid_length) is passed as explicit mutated tensor arguments and not through a layer_name lookup, so the planner sees the state's storage and dependencies. Gaps: there is no gated_delta_rule, causal_conv1d or SSM op. kv_attention handles one-token decode only (no multi-token verify for spec decode, no batched ragged decode). Scale is hard-coded to dim**-0.5, and other scales are folded into q, which adds a rounding point. Softcap and attention sinks fall back to eager or raise. Sliding window raises when capacity > window, because there is no ring buffer.

megabake_status.idea: Piecewise compilation and piecewise CUDA graphs
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake never needs to split for capture. A related missing piece is per-op fallback: an unsupported op (e.g. linalg_solve_triangular) fails the whole compile. vLLM's split-at-op design would allow megakernel | eager op | megakernel. That costs two launches, but compilation of new architectures would not fail.

megabake_status.idea: Dual-mode CUDA graphs with capability-based downgrade
megabake_status.evidence: compiler.py:410-423 (mode decode/prefill selection policy); buckets.py; benchmarks use separate decode and prefill backends
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake has a separate decode kernel and bucketed prefill kernels, which is the same split as FULL decode / PIECEWISE mixed. It has no per-op capability declaration (e.g. 'this body supports ragged batches' or 'multi-token') to drive automatic downgrade or fallback.

megabake_status.idea: Model-agnostic capture-size ladder and compile ranges
megabake_status.notes: Power-of-two buckets waste up to about 2x at bucket edges (a 65-token prompt pays for 128). vLLM's ladder has a step of 8 up to 256 and 16 above, which caps padding at 7-15 tokens, but needs about 67 captures. Each MegaBake bucket costs 24 s to 41 min to compile, so a dense ladder is not affordable. The way out is runtime token counts inside the kernel (see exclusive opportunities). MegaBake has no compile ranges (one dynamic-shape compile per range) because its kernels have static shapes.

megabake_status.evidence: compiler.py:410-423 (swapAB if all GEMMs <= 64 rows), planner.py:450-470 (mode-dependent body order)
megabake_status.notes: Decisions depend on size, but they are hard-coded thresholds inside body selection rather than declarative per-pass applicability over a token range. There is also no per-range choice of strategy (megakernel vs Inductor), which is the most valuable range gate for prefill.

megabake_status.idea: vLLM IR semantic ops with late priority-based lowering
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/regions.py:147-190,501-720,822-1010,2159-2330 (RMSNorm, RoPE, attention and gated MLP recognized from decomposed aten chains); regions.py is 2,538 lines
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake turns decomposed aten back into semantic regions (RegionCandidate with semantic_facts) and then picks bodies, so it has a semantic layer, but it is reached only by pattern recovery. The RMSNorm matcher expects exactly pow.Tensor_Scalar -> mean -> add -> rsqrt -> mul (regions.py:686-720). Variants such as x*x, var_mean, a (1+w) Gemma weight or a cast placed elsewhere need new code [uncertain which variants already fail]. MegaBake has no provider priority list or supports_args predicate. Body choice is a sort key in planner.py.

megabake_status.idea: CustomOp dual forms and matchers covering both
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/lowering.py:211-306 (reference impl doubles as eager fallback)
megabake_status.notes: Declared ops have a reference implementation, but the region matchers do not accept 'declared op OR decomposed equivalent' symmetrically except for attention (declared candidate plus decomposed _attention_candidate).

megabake_status.evidence: regions.py scalar-chain fusion, gated_mlp region, RMSNorm region; schedule.py:1383-1395 interval folding (recompute small producers); ROADMAP 4.2.3 (RMSNorm into GEMM prologue, residual/SiLU*mul into GEMM epilogue) not done; bias epilogue done (bodies/gemm.py:1925-1964)
megabake_status.notes: In a megakernel, a fusion does not need a new hand-written kernel. It can be done by scheduling, either by removing a barrier or by recomputing in the consumer's interval. MegaBake already does part of this with interval folding. MegaBake has no quantization yet, so quant fusions do not apply. The vLLM equivalents of add+RMSNorm and GEMM epilogue fusion are the next ones to take.

This becomes relevant if multi-GPU support is added. Inside a megakernel the allreduce can be fused at tile granularity with NVSHMEM or IPC signals (Mirage MPK does this), and that goes further than FlashInfer's single fused kernel.
Takeaway: vLLM dropped it, so it is not a model to copy. In a megakernel, per-tile overlap of communication and GEMM is the natural form of AsyncTP.

megabake_status.evidence: ROADMAP step 5 (views: select, squeeze, split->slice, unsqueeze, as primitive families); regions.py _index_map/_compose_index_maps:2436-2476 compose views into loads
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake folds views into index maps of loads, which is stronger than deleting identity reshapes. In-place input writes (copy_) are handled. [uncertain] whether slice_scatter of a full extent is always elided.

megabake_status.idea: Transformers-backend dataflow fusers (QKV merge, gate/up merge, RMSNorm detection)
megabake_status.evidence: grep for qkv/horizontal/sibling in src/megabake returns nothing; PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:79 'K and V fill 3 of 60 CTAs'
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake runs q, k and v as separate GEMM phases. They share a barrier interval, so they do run concurrently, but each pays its own pipeline start-up and tile-tail effects. Gate and up are separate GEMMs followed by a SiLU*mul phase. A generic FX-level horizontal GEMM fusion (several mm nodes on the same activation with constant weights, weights concatenated at compile time) would reproduce vLLM's QKV/GLU fusers without AST rewriting.

Features are switched by env vars and booleans, not by predicates on target or model facts. Split-K is off globally because it showed no gain on the 60-SM slice, when it should be decided per target and per GEMM shape.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: No splitting ops: stateful mixers run inside the same launch as the dense layers
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: vLLM must keep attention and SSM ops out of CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE) or limit FULL graphs to uniform decode, because their metadata and kernel choice depend on the batch composition on the host. Every piece boundary is a launch with a full drain and fill of the GPU. Even FULL graphs replay ~450-630 separate kernels (benchmarks: Inductor decode 458-632 launches), each with a tail and a ramp-up.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs plus PDL (griddepcontrol.launch_dependents/wait). PDL overlaps the next kernel's prologue with the previous kernel's tail, but only for adjacent kernels and only after the producer triggers. Data dependencies are still whole-kernel.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: Reading valid_length and token counts on the device (kv_attention already mutates valid_length on the device) lets one launch cover any context length. Decode attention phases can be linked to their QKV GEMM tiles by event counters (ROADMAP step 10) and not by grid barriers.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Fusion by scheduling instead of by fused-kernel authoring
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Every vLLM fusion (RMSNorm+quant, SiLU+quant, AllReduce+RMSNorm, RoPE+KV write, QK-norm+RoPE) needs a pattern and a hand-written fused CUDA/Triton/FlashInfer kernel, and the support matrix differs per platform (docs/design/fusions.md support table). Inductor fuses only pointwise and reduction work around template epilogues. In a graph of kernels, two ops that each need a different grid shape cannot share a kernel.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Inductor epilogue/prologue fusion into Triton templates, CUTLASS EVT epilogues, and hand-written fused kernels per pattern.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: Any producer-consumer pair can be fused by removing the grid barrier between them: an event dependency, recomputing the producer in the consumer's interval (already done by _fold_small_intervals), or running independent phases concurrently in the same interval. This works for any op family, so new architectures get fusion without new kernels. That is the generality argument for the megakernel.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A kernel cannot start streaming the next GEMM's weights while the current attention or norm runs unless it is resident. With CUDA graphs the next kernel launches only after its predecessor (or after the PDL trigger), so HBM idles during latency-bound phases (attention ~10 us/layer, RMSNorm ~2.8 us, barriers ~0.7 us).
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: A side-stream prefetch kernel issuing L2 prefetches (cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2) for the next layer's weights, or PDL prologues that prefetch. Both are limited by L2 capacity and stream ordering and are not tied to tile-level readiness.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: ROADMAP step 9: CTAs waiting on a barrier or an event issue L2 prefetches for their next GEMM tiles. A 1.7B layer's bf16 GEMM weights (4*2048^2 + 3*2048*8192 parameters, about 134 MB) are far larger than the slice's 29 MiB L2. Prefetch therefore has to be partial: the leading tiles of the next phase, so each GEMM starts with its pipeline already full.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Runtime token count without a capture ladder
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A CUDA graph freezes grid dimensions and kernel arguments, so vLLM captures about 67 sizes ([1,2,4]+8-step to 256 +16-step to 512) and pads every batch to the next size. Each capture costs memory and startup time.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Kernels with device-side bounds (FlashAttention varlen with cu_seqlens), persistent GEMMs with a device-read M, and coarse padding buckets.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: A persistent kernel with a fixed grid can read the token count from device memory and loop over ceil(n/tile) tiles per phase (Mirage's approach, noted in ROADMAP Gaps). One compiled kernel per coarse bucket (or one up to the maximum) then serves every length with no padding waste and no 41-minute compiles per extra bucket.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: State-aware planning across declared mixer ops
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: vLLM's mixer ops are opaque to the compiler: state sits behind layer_name, and the op must be a split boundary. The compiler cannot overlap the next layer's work with the mixer, and cannot place the mixer's KV write in the producer's epilogue unless someone writes a fused kernel (RoPE+KV-cache fusion exists only for ROCm AITER).
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Hand-written fused rope_kvcache and qk_norm_rope_kvcache kernels (ROCm only per fusions.md), and FlashInfer's fused KV append.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: Because MegaBake's declared ops carry explicit mutated state tensors, the planner can schedule the KV append as part of the RoPE/V-projection phase and let attention wait only on the tiles it reads.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Hiding communication at tile granularity (future multi-GPU)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion in vLLM is one fused kernel at a kernel boundary, enabled only below per-GPU size thresholds. Sequence parallelism and AsyncTP were removed. Overlapping collectives with GEMMs across kernels needs extra streams or collective-matmul kernels.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: FlashInfer trtllm fused allreduce, NCCL symmetric memory, and collective-matmul (AsyncTP) kernels.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.megabake_leverage: Per-tile signals between GPUs inside the persistent kernel (Mirage MPK NVSHMEM tasks) let the next layer's GEMM tiles start as soon as their reduced slice arrives.

measured_or_reported_gains: vLLM docs/design/fusions.md indicative end-to-end speedups (model, batch and hardware not specified): AllReduce+RMSNorm 5-20% (TP>1, low num_tokens); Attention+Quant 3-7%; RoPE+KV-cache 2-4% (ROCm); QK-norm+RoPE 2-3%; RMSNorm+Quant 1-4%; SiLU*Mul+Quant 1-4%; MLA dual RMSNorm 1-2%.

vLLM blog (2025-08-20, torch.compile): SiLU+FP8 quant fusion up to 8% throughput on Llama 3.1 405B FP8, 8x AMD MI300 (the quant overhead was about 8%, so this is the upper bound). Attention+Quant FP8 up to 7%, AllReduce+RMSNorm up to 15%, AllReduce+RMSNorm+FP8 up to 8%, +FP4 up to 10%, SP plus AsyncTP up to 10%. Configurations not stated [uncertain].

fusions.md:212 and 240: on NVIDIA, Inductor's generated RMSNorm+quant and SiLU+quant kernels are faster than vLLM's custom fused CUDA kernels. vLLM keeps its own fusions only where custom ops are forced, which shows that generated code can beat hand kernels on memory-bound ops.
No published vLLM number isolates piecewise vs full CUDA graphs. docs/design/cuda_graphs.md only calls FULL_AND_PIECEWISE 'generally the most performant'.

MegaBake measured (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18, H200 MIG 3g.71gb, batch 1, capacity 128): decode kernel GPU time 135M 1,502 us vs Inductor 1,382 us; 1.7B 2,974 vs 2,425 us; Qwen2-0.5B 1,584 vs 1,636 us. Decode complete call 135M 2,138 vs 11,925 us; 1.7B 3,311 vs 10,323 us (Inductor uses 458-632 launches). Prefill at 4 tokens: 1.7B 3,339 vs 3,060 us for Inductor with CUDA graphs.

MegaBake ROADMAP: 1.7B decode GEMMs 1.92 ms at about 1.8 TB/s. 49 RMSNorms at 2.8 us after the reduction-body fix. 24 decode attentions at about 10 us. Barrier 0.70 us. 135M decode barrier intervals went from 333 to 183 after folding.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Range-gated strategy choice for prefill (vLLM-style compile ranges): above a crossover token count measured at compile time, lower to Inductor+CUDA graphs (or a piecewise hybrid). Below it, keep the megakernel.
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: Prefill at 128-300 tokens is currently 3.1-21x slower than Inductor+CUDA graphs (1.7B: 16.7 ms vs 3.8 ms at 100 tokens, 158 ms vs 6.7 ms at 300). Routing those to Inductor brings them to parity right away, saving 13-150 ms per call. Decode is unchanged. This is not a megakernel gain, but it removes the worst regression while prefill bodies are rebuilt.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Residual-add + RMSNorm fused, and RMSNorm folded into the following GEMM's prologue (vLLM fused_add_rms_norm canonicalization; Mirage rmsnorm_linear)
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: 1.7B decode has 49 RMSNorm phases at about 2.8 us, plus a barrier interval each at 0.7 us, and the residual add phases. Recomputing the per-row rsqrt statistics inside each GEMM CTA (hidden 2048, 1 row = 4 KB, under 1 us of redundant work) removes the norm phase and its barrier: about 49*(2.8+0.7) = 0.17 ms, about 6% of the 2.97 ms kernel. On 135M (30 layers, 61 norms) about 0.2 ms of 1.5 ms, about 13%.
expected_impact_on_megabake.confidence: medium [uncertain: overlap within intervals makes per-phase attribution approximate]

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: SiLU*mul in the gate/up GEMM epilogue, using interleaved gate/up weights (vLLM GLUFuser / MergedColumnParallel)
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: Removes one elementwise phase and one barrier per layer: 24*(1.5-3 us + 0.7 us) = 0.05-0.09 ms on 1.7B (2-3%). It also merges two GEMM pipelines into one with twice the tile count, which helps tile balance on 60 SMs.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Horizontal QKV weight concatenation (generic FX pass: mm nodes sharing an activation input with constant weights)
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: q/k/v already share an interval, so the gain is pipeline start-up and tail: about 1-2 us per layer, roughly 0.03-0.05 ms on 1.7B (1-2%). It is larger on GQA models where K and V have only 1-3 tiles each (PERFORMANCE_REPORT: K and V fill 3 of 60 CTAs).

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Runtime token count in the persistent kernel instead of power-of-two padding (replaces the capture-size ladder)
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: Removes padding waste: on average about 25% of a power-of-two bucket and up to 2x at bucket edges (65 tokens pay for 128). The bigger payoff is compile time: one kernel per coarse range instead of 6 buckets (1.7B 512-bucket compile 41 min). Decode is unaffected.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: vLLM-IR-style semantic op layer plus provider priority and supports_args for body selection
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: No direct speed gain. Reduces new-architecture failures (Gemma 3 attention matching broke on a stride heuristic; Qwen3.5 fails on cumsum and triangular solve) and makes fusions like ranks 2-3 a single-node match.
expected_impact_on_megabake.confidence: high for generality, zero for latency

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Per-op fallback (split-at-op hybrid): megakernel | Inductor/eager op | megakernel
expected_impact_on_megabake.estimate: Costs about 2 extra launches (about 10-20 us of host/launch time per break). It turns 'compile failed' into 'runs, slightly slower' for architectures like Qwen3.5 until gated_delta_rule is declared.

vllm_how_it_stays_generic: Model code calls a small set of declared ops (attention, mixers, IR ops). Compiler passes match those single nodes, so one pattern covers every model that uses the layer. Model-specific knowledge sits in the model file and the op declaration, not in compiler matchers.
Capture sizes and compile ranges come only from engine limits (max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens, spec-decode width) and the device family, never from model shapes (config/vllm.py:2366-2580).
Fusion enablement is a predicate on hardware capability and model properties (config/vllm.py:150-229), with per-pass is_applicable_for_range.
CUDA graph mode is downgraded automatically from the attention backends' declared capability (AttentionCGSupport).
The Transformers backend uses dataflow fusers that match by FX structure, not by class names, and warns when a module named *RMSNorm does not match (fuser.py:85-97).
Kernel choice is a provider priority list with supports_args predicates (vllm/ir/op.py). Autotuning over providers is planned. Today flashinfer_autotune is the only autotuning at runtime.
vllm_own_overfitting: agent_space/vllm/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/*: epsilon is enumerated as [1e-5, 1e-6] in 11 places (e.g. rms_quant_fusion.py:787, add_rms_fusion.py:146, allreduce_rms_fusion.py:1070). A model with eps=1e-8 or 3e-6 silently gets no fusion.

agent_space/vllm/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py:104-130 hand-measured per-capability, per-world-size MB thresholds; removed SP thresholds SP_MIN_HIDDEN_SIZE=8192 and SP_MIN_PER_GPU_SIZE_MB={90:8,100:32}.

agent_space/vllm/vllm/config/compilation.py:768-788 _attention_ops lists model-specific op names (qwen4_exp_qsa, deepseek_v4_attention, olmo_hybrid_gdn_full_forward). Generality comes from every new architecture adding its own declared op.
Patterns are traced on bf16 example tensors (empty_bf16(5,16)). fp16 and fp32 coverage depends on separate registration [uncertain].

megabake_flags.item: SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64 and SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES=(16,32,64); the comment justifies them with 60-SM measurements (0.84-1.04 to 1.78-2.07 TB/s).
megabake_flags.risk: hw-specific: the crossover from swapAB to normal orientation depends on SM count, bandwidth and K. On a 132-SM H100/H200 or on SM100 it may move. It should be measured per target or derived from a tile-utilization cost model.

megabake_flags.item: SPLIT_K_MAX=16, SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES=2, and split-K disabled globally by env because it gave 'no gain on the 60-SM slice'.
megabake_flags.risk: hw-specific: a global off switch decided on one slice. On a full GPU, decode projections with fewer tiles than SMs are more common, so split-K is more likely to pay there. It should be a per-GEMM cost decision.

megabake_flags.item: swapAB is chosen per launch only if every GEMM has <= 64 rows (one shared-memory layout per launch).
megabake_flags.risk: Couples all GEMMs of a model. A model with one larger GEMM (e.g. lm_head with batch) flips the whole launch.

megabake_flags.item: small_m = rows <= 16 and small_tile = cta_shape[-1] <= 64 heuristics in body ordering.
megabake_flags.risk: Thresholds tuned to the tested decode shapes.
Hand-picked limits for interval folding. They should come from estimated phase cost against barrier cost (0.7 us, measured per target).
Model-agnostic, but the ladder is coarse and has no token-count cost model. vLLM derives its ladder from scheduler limits.

megabake_flags.item: Attention numerics policy hard-codes score/probability dtype torch.bfloat16.
megabake_flags.risk: Model-specific to bf16 checkpoints. fp16 or fp32 models get a wrong numerics contract [uncertain whether this is checked downstream].

megabake_flags.item: kv_attention is one-token only, scale is fixed at dim**-0.5 (other scales folded into q), softcap and sinks unsupported, sliding window raises when capacity > window.
megabake_flags.risk: Excludes Gemma 2 (softcap), gpt-oss (sinks), long-context sliding-window models and spec-decode verification.

megabake_flags.item: RMSNorm recognized only as pow.Tensor_Scalar -> mean -> add -> rsqrt -> mul with an optional convert.
megabake_flags.risk: Brittle decomposed-pattern matching of the kind vLLM avoids with semantic ops and dataflow fusers. Variants (x*x, var_mean, (1+w) scaling order, fp32 weight multiply) may miss and fall back to slower generic regions. MegaBake extracts epsilon as a value, which is better than vLLM's enumerated eps.

megabake_flags.item: TargetFacts lacks HBM bandwidth, L2 size, clock and barrier cost.
megabake_flags.risk: Without them no cost model is possible, so decisions end up as constants measured on the MIG slice (see above). Clocks on the shared slice vary from 345 to 1,980 MHz, so any measured constant is noisy.

megabake_flags.item: Fixed relative-L2 acceptance limits of 0.01 and 0.02.
megabake_flags.risk: Depth- and dtype-dependent. ROADMAP 2.3 already shows that global tolerances confuse rounding with bugs. vLLM uses per-op, per-dtype tolerances (ir/ops/layernorm.py:40,66).

megabake_flags.item: Body evidence measured=False and require_measured unused by default.
megabake_flags.risk: Selection is not backed by per-target measurements, so tuned bodies are assumed good on every target.

generality_and_overfitting_risk.how_to_avoid: Put every threshold behind a cost model that reads TargetFacts (SM count, bandwidth, L2, measured barrier cost). Where the model is unsure, run a short on-device autotune at compile time over two or three candidates (swapAB vs not, split-K count, fold vs not) and cache the result keyed on the target. Copy vLLM's provider priority with supports_args for bodies, and match semantic ops with scalar wildcards (epsilon, scale) rather than enumerated constants. Validate on at least one non-tested architecture family (Gemma 2/3, Phi, Mistral sliding window, a hybrid SSM) and on a full-GPU configuration (132 SMs) before freezing any default.

hardware_portability: Generic across SM80, SM90 and SM100: declared ops, the semantic op layer, compile ranges and buckets, range-gated strategy choice, no-op and view folding, horizontal weight concatenation, cache keys, residual+RMSNorm recompute in consumer phases, and runtime token counts. These are compiler and IR ideas with no hardware dependence. SM90-specific in MegaBake's current implementations: the swapAB TMA/WGMMA GEMM (WGMMA M=64 is what makes swapAB necessary), TMA descriptors written in the table prologue, and cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for prefetch. On SM100, tcgen05 MMA with TMEM accumulators and 2-CTA MMA (M=128/256) change the small-M picture. swapAB is still needed, but tile choices and thresholds differ, and CLC (cluster launch control) offers hardware work-stealing that could replace part of the persistent scheduler. On SM80 there is no TMA or WGMMA: GEMMs use cp.async + mma.sync, swapAB matters less (mma.sync M=16), and L2 prefetch has to use prefetch.global.L2 per thread. vLLM's own portability approach is platform dispatch keys and per-platform forward_* methods, provider supports flags, and capability-gated predicates (is_device_capability(90), family(100)), with per-capability tables for thresholds. MegaBake should keep the scheduler, IR and fusion target-independent, select bodies through providers declaring (target, supports_args, cost), and keep every numeric threshold either in TargetFacts-derived formulas or in a per-target tuned cache, never in module constants.

recommended_actions.action: Add a compile-range strategy gate: for each mode and bucket, compile both the megakernel and Inductor+CUDA graphs at a probe size, measure both, and route token ranges above the measured crossover to Inductor. Record the crossover in the plan cache keyed by (model graph hash, target).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Prefill 128-300 tokens from 3-21x slower to parity with Inductor+CUDA graphs. Decode unchanged.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: None; the whole-invocation inductor fallback already exists.

recommended_actions.action: Canonicalize residual-add + RMSNorm into one semantic region (vLLM fused_add_rms_norm) and allow RMSNorm to be recomputed in the prologue of the consuming GEMM phase (per-row statistics recomputed per CTA).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: About 0.17 ms (6%) on 1.7B decode and about 0.2 ms (13%) on 135M decode [uncertain]. Closes most of the gap to Inductor's kernel time on 135M.
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/regions.py (_rms_norm_candidate, new fused_add_rms_norm family), src/megabake/bodies/gemm.py (prologue hook), src/megabake/schedule.py (recompute into GEMM consumer)
recommended_actions.prerequisite: GEMM body accepting a per-row scale vector on the A operand (or the B operand under swapAB).

recommended_actions.action: Generic horizontal GEMM fusion pass: mm/addmm nodes with the same activation input and constant weights get their weights concatenated at compile time (QKV, gate/up), with SiLU*mul (or any elementwise binary of the two halves) moved into the merged GEMM epilogue via interleaved columns.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: 0.08-0.14 ms on 1.7B decode (3-5%) combined [uncertain]. Fewer phases, tiles and barriers per layer.
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/frontend.py or graph.py (new pre-region pass), src/megabake/regions.py (_gated_mlp_candidate), src/megabake/bodies/gemm.py (epilogue)
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Weights must be parameters (constant), as in compiled inference.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a semantic-op layer like vLLM IR: register megabake semantic ops (rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, rope, silu_and_mul, attention, kv_attention, gated_delta_rule, causal_conv1d) with a reference, a fake implementation and per-dtype tolerances. Recognize them with dataflow matchers in which scalars (eps, scale) are wildcards, and optionally with HF module-level fusers like vLLM's Transformers backend. Select bodies through a provider priority list with supports_args.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Generality: one matcher per op family, fewer silent misses on new architectures, and per-op tolerance replaces the global L2 limit.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: None; can migrate one family at a time (RMSNorm first).

recommended_actions.action: Declare megabake::gated_delta_rule and megabake::causal_conv1d with explicit state tensors (as ROADMAP step 6). Until bodies exist, support a per-op split fallback (megakernel | eager op | megakernel) so Qwen3.5 compiles.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Qwen3.5-0.8B goes from compile failure to running. Hybrid models get coverage.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Graph splitting at declared ops (vLLM split_graph-style) for the fallback path.

recommended_actions.action: Extend kv_attention to take scale, softcap, sinks, sliding-window ring buffer and q_len > 1 (spec-decode verify, chunked decode), and declare which capabilities each attention body supports (like AttentionCGSupport) so unsupported cases fall back automatically.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Coverage for Gemma 2/3, gpt-oss and Mistral-style sliding window. No more extra rounding from folding the scale into q.

recommended_actions.action: Replace hard-coded tuning constants with TargetFacts-driven cost formulas and a cached compile-time micro-autotune: swapAB row limit, split-K count, fold limits, small-M thresholds. Add hbm_bandwidth, l2_bytes, measured barrier_us and clock to TargetFacts.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Avoids regressions on full-size GPUs and SM100. Split-K may turn positive on 132-SM parts [uncertain].
recommended_actions.prerequisite: A stable timing harness that handles the shared-slice clock variance (clock ramp, back-to-back comparison).

recommended_actions.action: Runtime token count inside the persistent kernel (device-read n; per-phase tile loops bounded by ceil(n/tile)), so one kernel serves a range rather than a padded bucket.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Removes up to 2x padding at bucket edges and cuts the number of compiled buckets, reducing multi-minute compiles.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Event counters in the table launch (step 10) make dynamic tile counts easier to synchronize.

recommended_actions.action: Include matcher, body and catalog source hashes in the plan cache key (as vLLM pass uuids do).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Correctness and hygiene. Prevents stale plans after compiler edits.
